author: L0din_
quote:
GTA VI is a **** chore simulator. I sank a **** of time into it, more than ten hours, before it finally reminded me why I downloaded it. And even then, only for a bit. Paint this wall. Go buy some flowers. Then they finally let you steal a car, shoot some ****, and raise hell. You barely have time to think “**** finally” before the game grabs you by the scruff of the neck and drags you back into the story. Why the **** do I have to wait this long to play GTA in GTA?

And the whole **** time, somebody’s talking. They talk in the car, they talk while you’re trudging along behind them, they talk in cutscenes. When the whole mission is driving to a waypoint while they have yet another conversation, by the time we get there I’ve already forgotten where we’re going. I just want them both to shut the **** up.

Jason’s dumb as a stump. I haven’t played a game in a long time where I wanted so badly to be playing as literally anyone else. Lucia gets on my nerves too, and I still have no idea what either of them actually wants. They go out to rob a few shops and pick a **** waffle joint. Of all the places they could rob, why the **** a waffle joint? Fine, they get a kick out of robbing places. Why should I spend another few dozen hours watching where that takes them?

**** the story for a minute. What is there to do in the open world? Play a console game inside the game I’m already playing on my console? Shoot some pool? The way people gush about these minigames, you’d think they’d never played a GTA before. But hey, now you can keep tabs on your car’s condition and get it delivered through Scooter Bros. A regular delivery costs in-game cash, and the in-game Premium upgrade gives you three free deliveries per in-game day. Why the **** am I working out car delivery rates in GTA? I just wanted to drive the damn thing.

And here’s Rockstar trying to show us the future of open-world games on a console generation that started in 2020. By the time GTA VI came out, the base PS5 was already six years old, and a high-end gaming PC could do more even back then. I fire it up on a PS5 Pro, and even on the Pro it looks like the same **** smeary mess. I turn the camera and it feels like someone’s rubbing sandpaper across my eyes. Jesus **** Christ, it looks so bad I physically want to look away.

Eleven **** years. That’s roughly how long it’s been since work on the game started. What the **** is in this game that took eleven years to make? Yeah, the world’s huge. Yeah, they put a lot of work into the little details. And somehow it still feels like I’m playing a **** mash-up of Red Dead Redemption, The Sims, and some random GTA clone. Which is pretty **** funny considering I booted up GTA itself.

Real life already has enough **** that makes me go “****, this again.” I boot up GTA to have fun. By the time this game finally let me cut loose for a bit, I was already wondering if I’d bother turning it on the next day. If I ever give a **** how it ends, I’ll watch the ending on YouTube. I’m sure as **** not playing this **** twice.
